props.heading: Best trips from Miami on a budget
props.subheading: Real flight, hotel, and activity costs for the destinations that actually fit what you have to spend — flying out of MIA.

props.text: Miami is the biggest U.S. gateway to Latin America and the Caribbean — Cancún from MIA is the shortest hop to Cancún of any hub we cover. Flying out of MIA, a trip to Oaxaca can start around $1,130 for flight, hotel, and activities together — not just the flight, pulled from our own cost data, not guesses.

features.title: Cancún — nonstop, ~1h55m
features.text: American flies it nonstop 4–6 times a day — the fastest Cancún route out of any hub on this site.

features.title: Oaxaca — no nonstop
features.text: Routes via Mexico City on American or Aeroméxico, roughly 7.5 hours total — even Miami's huge Latin America network doesn't reach this smaller regional airport directly.

features.title: Grand Cayman — nonstop, ~1h40m–1h51m
features.text: Both American and Cayman Airways fly it direct — English-speaking and USD-friendly on arrival, with no currency exchange to think about.

props.text: American alone serves roughly 100 destinations across Latin America and the Caribbean from Miami — the deepest network of any hub we cover — which is why Cancún and Grand Cayman are both quick, easy nonstops. Oaxaca is the honest exception: it's a smaller regional airport that even Miami's reach doesn't connect to directly, so it routes through Mexico City instead.

items.question: Are these real-time prices?
items.answer: They're estimates based on our own curated cost data for this route and season, not a live quote — the real price on the partner site may be a bit higher or lower depending on exact dates.

items.question: Why is there no direct Miami–Oaxaca flight given Miami's huge Latin America network?
items.answer: Oaxaca is a smaller regional airport — even Miami's extensive network routes through Mexico City instead, adding up to roughly 7.5 hours total.

items.question: Is Grand Cayman easy to reach from Miami?
items.answer: Yes — under 2 hours nonstop on two different airlines, and it's English-speaking with USD widely accepted, so there's less to plan around on arrival.
